findings.summary: Audited the UI/responsiveness/consistency dimension of the NCPL analytics web app (apps/web): layout shell (Shell.tsx, Sidebar.tsx, Topbar.tsx/TopbarClient.tsx), design tokens (globals.css), reusable primitives (KpiCard, ChartCard, DataTable, EmptyState, PageHeader, card.tsx, badge.tsx, sheet.tsx, Skeletons), charts (AreaChart, BarChart, DonutChart, Sparkline, ChartTheme.ts), and dashboard pages (page.tsx/loading.tsx, people, compare, anomalies, etc.). Overall the design system is coherent (consistent HSL token usage, dark/light parity, tabular-nums in tables, responsive sm/md/lg/xl grids, mobile Sheet nav) but there are real defects: a broken SVG gradient id in Sparkline that almost certainly breaks KPI sparkline fills, two shared components (EmptyState, DataTable) that are essentially dead because nearly every page hand-rolls its own empty-state and table markup with divergent styling, a loading skeleton whose grid does not match the page it covers (layout shift / CLS), and the mobile nav dropping the workspace filter query string that the desktop sidebar preserves. Visual rendering and contrast items are marked Needs-runtime since I cannot exercise the live UI.

bugs.title: Sparkline gradient id contains hsl() string — invalid SVG id breaks the fill via url() reference
bugs.steps: 1. Open any page with KpiCards that pass a sparkline + sparklineColor, e.g. /dashboard (Command Center) 'Active users' and 'Events' KPIs which pass sparklineColor={CHART_COLORS.primary} / CHART_COLORS.emerald. 2. Inspect the rendered <linearGradient> element and the <Area fill> attribute.
bugs.expected: The area sparkline renders with its gradient fill.
bugs.actual: Sparkline builds the gradient id from the raw color string: id={`sparkGrad-${color}`} and fill={`url(#sparkGrad-${color})`} (Sparkline.tsx lines 17 and 27). CHART_COLORS values are full hsl literals like 'hsl(217 91% 60%)' (ChartTheme.ts lines 6-12). This yields id='sparkGrad-hsl(217 91% 60%)' and url(#sparkGrad-hsl(217 91% 60%)). The parentheses/spaces/percent make the url() reference fail to resolve (an unescaped '(' terminates the fragment), so the gradient fill does not apply — the sparkline area shows no fill. Additionally, two KpiCards using the same color produce duplicate DOM ids on the same page (id collision).
bugs.fix: Do not embed the color in the id. Use a React useId() (or a sanitized/hashed token) for the gradient id, e.g. const gradId = useId(); then id={gradId} and fill={`url(#${gradId})`}. This guarantees a valid, unique id per instance.
bugs.evidence: apps/web/src/components/charts/Sparkline.tsx:17,27 (id and url built from `color`); apps/web/src/components/charts/ChartTheme.ts:5-15 (colors are 'hsl(...)' literals); apps/web/src/components/analytics/KpiCard.tsx:53-60 + apps/web/src/app/(dashboard)/dashboard/page.tsx:75-84 (sparklineColor passed as CHART_COLORS literals).

bugs.title: Dashboard loading skeleton grid does not match the page it stands in for (layout shift / CLS)
bugs.steps: 1. Navigate to /dashboard and observe the streaming/loading state. 2. Compare the skeleton layout to the loaded layout.
bugs.expected: The loading skeleton mirrors the real page structure so content does not jump when data arrives.
bugs.actual: loading.tsx renders a KPI section of 4 skeleton cards at `grid sm:grid-cols-2 xl:grid-cols-4` and a 3-chart row. The real page renders 6 KPI cards at `grid sm:grid-cols-2 lg:grid-cols-3 xl:grid-cols-6`, a full-width applications table, a 2/3 + 1/3 chart row (`xl:grid-cols-3` with `xl:col-span-2`), and an activity feed. The count (4 vs 6), the column breakpoints, and the overall section structure differ, so the page visibly reflows/jumps when it hydrates.
bugs.fix: Update loading.tsx to match the real layout: 6 KpiCardSkeletons at `grid gap-4 sm:grid-cols-2 lg:grid-cols-3 xl:grid-cols-6`, a full-width table skeleton, and a `xl:grid-cols-3` chart row with a 2-span chart skeleton + 1-span chart skeleton, plus an activity/list skeleton.
bugs.evidence: apps/web/src/app/(dashboard)/dashboard/loading.tsx:14-23 (4 cards, xl:grid-cols-4) vs apps/web/src/app/(dashboard)/dashboard/page.tsx:74-90 (6 cards, sm:grid-cols-2 lg:grid-cols-3 xl:grid-cols-6) and 154-183 (xl:grid-cols-3 layout).

bugs.title: Mobile nav drops the workspace (app/project) filter query string that the desktop sidebar preserves
bugs.steps: 1. On desktop, select an Application/Project in the topbar workspace filter (adds ?app=...&project=... to the URL). 2. Shrink to mobile width (<md) so the sidebar is hidden and the hamburger Sheet menu is used. 3. Tap any nav item in the Sheet.
bugs.expected: Navigating preserves the selected app/project filter, identical to desktop behavior.
bugs.actual: The desktop Sidebar deliberately appends the preserved filter query string to every link (Sidebar.tsx lines 20-28 build queryString; line 58 href={`${item.href}${queryString}`}). The mobile Sheet nav in TopbarClient links with bare `href={item.href}` (line 62), so navigating from the mobile menu silently resets the workspace filter. Inconsistent behavior between viewports.
bugs.fix: Reuse the same query-string preservation in the mobile nav (read useSearchParams in TopbarClient and build the same app/project query string, or extract a shared helper) and append it to each mobile Link href.
bugs.evidence: apps/web/src/components/layout/Sidebar.tsx:20-28,58 (preserves ?app/?project); apps/web/src/components/layout/TopbarClient.tsx:60-63 (href={item.href} with no query string).

bugs.title: Shared EmptyState component is unused — every page hand-rolls divergent empty states
bugs.steps: 1. Grep the codebase for EmptyState imports. 2. Compare empty-state markup across pages (people, compare, anomalies, audience, features, etc.).
bugs.expected: A single reusable EmptyState drives consistent padding, icon treatment, and typography for all 'no data' states.
bugs.actual: EmptyState.tsx exists (icon-in-circle, p-10, rounded-lg, max-w-sm description) but is imported by zero pages (only the file itself matches). Pages instead hand-roll empty states with inconsistent styling: DataTable.tsx and ActivityFeed.tsx use `border border-dashed p-8 text-center text-sm`; people/compare/anomalies use `border border-dashed bg-muted/30 p-8` with an icon circle that is sometimes h-10 w-10 (people/compare) and sometimes a colored bg-emerald-500/15 (anomalies); some have no icon at all. Padding (p-8 vs p-10), rounding (rounded-md vs rounded-lg), and icon presence all diverge.
bugs.fix: Replace the hand-rolled empty-state blocks with the shared EmptyState component (passing icon/title/description/action), and have DataTable/ActivityFeed render EmptyState for their empty branch. Delete the bespoke markup so styling stays consistent.
bugs.evidence: Grep for 'EmptyState' returns only apps/web/src/components/shared/EmptyState.tsx; hand-rolled empties at apps/web/src/components/analytics/DataTable.tsx:20-21, ActivityFeed.tsx:13-14, app/(dashboard)/dashboard/people/page.tsx:57-65 & 134-145, compare/page.tsx:75-86, anomalies/page.tsx:86-96.

bugs.title: Shared DataTable component used by only one page; ~9 pages hand-roll tables with different typography/spacing
bugs.steps: 1. Grep for DataTable imports. 2. Compare table markup between users/page.tsx and people/compare/page.tsx.
bugs.expected: Tables share one component so header casing, font size, cell padding, hover, and overflow behavior are consistent platform-wide.
bugs.actual: DataTable (text-sm, px-4 py-2.5 header / px-4 py-3 cells, bg-muted/40 thead, divide-y, overflow-x-auto wrapper) is imported only by app/(dashboard)/dashboard/users/page.tsx. The Command Center table, people, compare, and other pages hand-roll <table className='w-full text-xs'> with px-2 py-2 cells and a plain `text-muted-foreground` thead — visibly smaller text and tighter spacing than the DataTable standard. Same data-grid concept, two different visual languages.
bugs.fix: Migrate the hand-rolled tables to the DataTable component (it already supports column align, render, rowKey, and empty text), or align the inline tables to DataTable's tokens (text-sm, px-4 py-3, bg-muted/40 header). Pick one and apply everywhere.
bugs.evidence: Only apps/web/src/app/(dashboard)/dashboard/users/page.tsx:3 imports DataTable; inline tables at app/(dashboard)/dashboard/page.tsx:111-149, people/page.tsx:68-98 & 148-178, compare/page.tsx:94-135 use text-xs/px-2 py-2 — differing from DataTable.tsx:24-63 (text-sm/px-4).

bugs.title: AreaChart/BarChart negative left margin can clip Y-axis tick labels for wide values
bugs.steps: 1. Render a chart whose Y values format to wide strings (e.g. large counts, percentages, or thousands with separators). 2. Observe the leftmost Y-axis tick labels.
bugs.expected: Y-axis tick labels are fully visible.
bugs.actual: Both charts set margin={{ ... left: -8 }} (AreaChart.tsx:38, BarChart.tsx:34) while YAxis width is fixed at 48 (lines 61 / 41). The negative left margin pulls the axis area left to reduce the gutter; combined with a fixed 48px axis width, multi-digit/formatted tick labels (e.g. '1,200', '100%') can be clipped at the container's left edge. This is a visual risk that depends on the formatted value width.
bugs.fix: Remove the negative left margin (use left: 0) or increase YAxis width to comfortably fit the widest formatted tick; verify with the largest expected formatY output.
bugs.evidence: apps/web/src/components/charts/AreaChart.tsx:38,56-62; apps/web/src/components/charts/BarChart.tsx:34,37-43.

bugs.title: Mobile nav Sheet has no SheetDescription / aria-describedby (Radix Dialog a11y warning)
bugs.steps: 1. Open the mobile hamburger menu (Sheet) at <md width. 2. Observe the console.
bugs.expected: Radix Dialog content has an accessible description (or aria-describedby={undefined} set intentionally); no console warning.
bugs.actual: SheetContent renders SheetHeader + SheetTitle but no SheetDescription (TopbarClient.tsx:43-46). Radix's Dialog (sheet.tsx wraps @radix-ui/react-dialog) emits a console warning when Description is missing and aria-describedby is not explicitly disabled. Minor a11y/console-noise issue.
bugs.fix: Add a visually-hidden SheetDescription (e.g. 'Primary navigation') inside the SheetHeader, or pass aria-describedby={undefined} to DialogPrimitive.Content if a description is genuinely not wanted.

bugs.title: Event category colors are defined twice with mismatched hues (chart tokens vs badge styles)
bugs.steps: 1. Compare the donut/category chart colors on /dashboard (uses CATEGORY_COLOR) with the EventBadge pills shown in the activity feed for the same categories.
bugs.expected: A given event category (e.g. 'auth', 'interaction') uses one consistent color across charts and badges.
bugs.actual: CATEGORY_COLOR maps auth→primary 'hsl(217 91% 60%)' (blue), interaction→secondary 'hsl(262 83% 64%)' (violet) (ChartTheme.ts:22-29). EventBadge.tsx independently hardcodes Tailwind palette classes: auth→blue-500, interaction→violet-500, navigation→sky-500, etc. (EventBadge.tsx:5-12). These are close but separately maintained sources of truth using different color systems (custom HSL vs Tailwind defaults), so the donut slice for a category and its badge can read as slightly different shades, and they can drift apart over time.
bugs.fix: Derive both from a single category-color source. Either drive EventBadge from CATEGORY_COLOR (inline style/CSS var) or document that the Tailwind classes must mirror the CHART_COLORS hues; centralize to avoid drift.
bugs.evidence: apps/web/src/components/charts/ChartTheme.ts:22-29 (CATEGORY_COLOR) vs apps/web/src/components/analytics/EventBadge.tsx:5-12 (CATEGORY_STYLES with hardcoded Tailwind colors).

recommendations: Fix the Sparkline gradient id (use React useId() instead of embedding the hsl color string) — this is the highest-impact visual bug since it likely blanks every KPI sparkline fill and can create duplicate DOM ids.

Rewrite app/(dashboard)/dashboard/loading.tsx to mirror the real Command Center layout (6 KPI cards at sm:grid-cols-2 lg:grid-cols-3 xl:grid-cols-6, a full-width table skeleton, and a 2-span + 1-span chart row) to eliminate layout shift.

Adopt the existing shared primitives that are currently dead code: route all 'no data' branches through components/shared/EmptyState and all data grids through components/analytics/DataTable (or align the inline tables to DataTable's text-sm/px-4 tokens). This removes the biggest source of cross-page inconsistency.
Make the mobile Sheet nav preserve the workspace filter query string exactly like Sidebar.tsx; extract the queryString builder into a shared hook/util so the two navs cannot drift.
Centralize event-category colors so EventBadge and CATEGORY_COLOR derive from one source, preventing chart vs badge color drift.
Reconsider the negative left chart margin (left: -8) or widen the YAxis to guarantee tick labels are never clipped for large/formatted values.
Add a visually-hidden SheetDescription (or explicit aria-describedby) to the mobile nav Sheet to clear the Radix Dialog a11y warning.
Run a runtime pass (responsive breakpoints, dark/light contrast, wide-table horizontal scroll on mobile) — these were marked Needs-runtime and should be verified in a browser before sign-off.

findings.summary: UX audit of the NCPL analytics platform (Next.js 15 App Router). Examined config/navigation.ts, the Command Center (app/(dashboard)/dashboard/page.tsx), People list + per-user profile, the global filter system (hooks/useFilters.ts, WorkspaceFilter, RangePicker), data fetchers with mock fallback (lib/data/fetchers.ts, lib/mock/dashboard.ts), the admin onboarding page, and shared empty-state primitives. Overall verdict: the IA, plain-English copy, and empty-state guidance for the People/Admin areas are genuinely strong, and clicks-to-value is short. But there are serious trust and consistency problems. The single biggest issue: the entire dashboard silently falls back to fabricated mock data (fake people with @ncpl.internal emails, invented KPIs) on ANY backend error, with a permanent "● Live" badge and zero indication the numbers are fake — a CEO Command Center that lies. The second systemic issue: the topbar exposes global Application / Project / Date-range filters on every page, but only 3 of ~17 pages actually read searchParams, so the headline Command Center and most pages ignore the filters entirely while still showing them as active — a broken-affordance / trust problem. Several smaller issues: a non-functional search box, an unused shared EmptyState (inconsistent hand-rolled empties), redundant/incorrect name-fallback logic, and the global Project filter being effectively dead. Most rendering claims are Needs-runtime since I cannot drive the live UI.

bugs.title: Dashboard silently shows fabricated mock data while displaying a permanent "● Live" badge (trust/integrity)
bugs.steps: 1. Run the app without a reachable Supabase backend, with an RLS denial, or any transient query error. 2. Open /dashboard (Command Center). 3. Observe KPIs (Active users, Logins, Sessions, Events, Errors, Health), the per-app health table, charts, and the 'Latest activity' feed.
bugs.expected: If live data cannot be fetched, the UI should clearly tell the user the data is unavailable or is sample/demo data — never present invented numbers as real, especially under a 'Live' badge in a CEO-facing Command Center.
bugs.actual: withMockFallback() in lib/data/fetchers.ts catches ANY error from the live repository and returns mock data with only a log.debug — no UI signal. mockDashboardKpis/mockEventsTimeSeries/mockRecentActivity fabricate plausible numbers and fake people (e.g. 'Aanya Reddy' with user1@ncpl.internal in lib/mock/dashboard.ts:120-157,177-182). The page (page.tsx:66-71) always renders a green '● Live' badge and the Topbar (TopbarClient.tsx:99-101) shows another '● Live' badge, so fabricated data looks like a live production feed. A CEO could make decisions on invented metrics.
bugs.fix: Make withMockFallback return a discriminated result ({ data, source: 'live' | 'mock' }) or set a request-scoped flag when any fallback fires. Render a prominent, persistent banner ('Showing sample data — not connected to live analytics') and suppress/replace the 'Live' badge whenever any fetch fell back. Gate mock fallback behind an explicit env flag (e.g. NCPL_ALLOW_MOCK=1) so production never silently fabricates. At minimum, log at warn/error, not debug.
bugs.evidence: apps/web/src/lib/data/fetchers.ts:105-135 (generic catch -> mock, log.debug only); apps/web/src/lib/mock/dashboard.ts:53-62,120-157,177-182 (fabricated KPIs + fake named users with @ncpl.internal emails); apps/web/src/app/(dashboard)/dashboard/page.tsx:66-71 (hardcoded Live badge); apps/web/src/components/layout/TopbarClient.tsx:99-101 (second hardcoded Live badge).

bugs.title: Global topbar filters (Application / Project / Range) are ignored by the Command Center and ~14 of 17 pages
bugs.module: components/layout/WorkspaceFilter.tsx, RangePicker.tsx, hooks/useFilters.ts vs. dashboard pages
bugs.steps: 1. Open /dashboard. 2. In the topbar, pick a specific Application (e.g. 'Sentinel') and a Date range (e.g. 'Last 7 days'). 3. Observe the URL gains ?app=...&range=... and the Command Center content.
bugs.expected: Selecting an Application or Range in the always-visible global filter should scope the data on the current page, as the copy in WorkspaceFilter.tsx promises ('the chosen scope flows into every downstream dashboard via URL state').
bugs.actual: CommandCenterPage (page.tsx:45-54) accepts no searchParams and calls fetchers with no filter args, so app/project/range selections change the URL but nothing on the page. A grep shows only 3 pages read searchParams at all (people, journeys, audience), and even those only read partial filters. The filter is a prominent, persistent affordance that does nothing on the landing page — users assume their selection applied and trust the unfiltered numbers.
bugs.fix: Either (a) thread app/project/range from searchParams into every page's fetchers (preferred), or (b) scope the filter UI per-page — only render the Application/Range controls on pages that honor them, and disable/hide them elsewhere with a tooltip. Add automated coverage asserting each page consumes the filters it displays.
bugs.evidence: apps/web/src/app/(dashboard)/dashboard/page.tsx:45-54 (no searchParams, no filter args); apps/web/src/components/layout/WorkspaceFilter.tsx:13-19 (promises scope flows downstream); apps/web/src/components/layout/RangePicker.tsx:7-12 (promises pages read range); grep of app/(dashboard) finds searchParams only in people, journeys, audience pages.

bugs.title: Global Project filter is effectively dead — populated from event metadata only, and no page filters by project
bugs.steps: 1. Open any dashboard page. 2. Inspect the second topbar select ('All projects'). 3. With no events carrying metadata.projectId, the dropdown shows only 'No projects yet' and is disabled. 4. Even when projects exist, selecting one (?project=) changes no page.
bugs.expected: A top-level filter shown on every screen should drive at least one view, and should not be disabled/empty for the common case.
bugs.actual: listProjects (workspace.ts:42-73) derives projects by scanning up to 5000 events for metadata.projectId — for a typical event-driven setup with no projectId metadata it returns [], so the select is permanently disabled ('No projects yet'). No page reads the project searchParam at all, so even a non-empty selection is inert. This is a confusing always-present control that never works.
bugs.fix: Remove the Project select from the topbar until at least one page consumes it, or source projects from the analytics_projects registry (already used by listApplications) and wire ?project= into the relevant pages. If kept disabled, add a tooltip explaining when projects appear.
bugs.evidence: apps/web/src/lib/repositories/workspace.ts:42-73 (project list from event metadata->projectId); apps/web/src/components/layout/WorkspaceFilter.tsx:53-63 (disabled + 'No projects yet'); no searchParams reader for 'project' anywhere under app/(dashboard).

bugs.title: Topbar search box is non-functional (decorative input with no behavior)
bugs.steps: 1. Open any dashboard page on desktop. 2. Click the 'Search applications, users, events…' input. 3. Type a query and press Enter.
bugs.expected: Either a working search (navigates to results / filters) or no search affordance at all.
bugs.actual: The <input type="search"> in TopbarClient.tsx:87-95 has no value, onChange, onSubmit, form, or handler. Typing does nothing and Enter does nothing. A prominent search bar that silently fails is a discoverability and trust problem (users assume the platform has search and that nothing matched).
bugs.fix: Implement minimal client-side search (route to People / Applications filtered by query) or remove the input until search exists. If deferred, mark it disabled with a 'Coming soon' placeholder so it doesn't read as broken.
bugs.evidence: apps/web/src/components/layout/TopbarClient.tsx:87-95 (input has no state or handlers).

bugs.title: Shared EmptyState component is unused; every page hand-rolls its own empty state with inconsistent copy/markup
bugs.steps: Compare empty states across Command Center app table, People (two variants), People detail, Admin Projects, and ActivityFeed.
bugs.expected: A single, consistent empty-state pattern (icon + title + guidance + CTA), ideally the shared EmptyState primitive.
bugs.actual: EmptyState.tsx exists with a clean API (icon/title/description/action) but a grep shows it is imported nowhere. Instead each surface re-implements empties differently: Command Center app table (page.tsx:102-110), People CrossApp (people/page.tsx:134-145), People AppDirectory (people/page.tsx:57-65), People detail apps/recent ('No app activity' / 'No recent activity', [userId]/page.tsx:110,134), Admin (projects/page.tsx:52-56), ActivityFeed default ('No activity in the last 5 minutes.'). Inconsistent voice, sizing, and some have no CTA.
bugs.fix: Adopt EmptyState across these surfaces (with an optional action prop for CTAs like 'Onboard an app'), or delete it if intentionally abandoned. Standardize copy and add a next-step CTA to every empty state.
bugs.evidence: apps/web/src/components/shared/EmptyState.tsx:13 (defined, exported); grep for 'EmptyState' matches only its own file; hand-rolled empties at app/(dashboard)/dashboard/page.tsx:102-110, people/page.tsx:57-65 & 134-145, people/[userId]/page.tsx:110 & 134, admin/projects/page.tsx:52-56.

bugs.title: User-detail name fallback is redundant/dead and never reaches the intended 'Anonymous user' label cleanly
bugs.steps: Open a user-detail page for an anonymous (no-email, no-displayName) user.
bugs.expected: Title shows a clear 'Anonymous user' (or similar) when there is no name/email.
bugs.actual: Line 48: const name = u.displayName ?? u.email ?? (u.email ? u.email : 'Anonymous user'); The third operand is unreachable — if u.email is nullish the second ?? already short-circuits to the parenthesized expr, where u.email is again nullish so it returns 'Anonymous user', but the (u.email ? u.email : ...) ternary is dead code (u.email is always falsy at that point). Works by accident but is confusing and brittle. The People list uses a different fallback ('Anonymous' vs 'Anonymous user'), so the same user shows two labels across screens.
bugs.fix: Simplify to: const name = u.displayName ?? u.email ?? 'Anonymous user'; and standardize the anonymous label across the People list (people/page.tsx:84,164 use 'Anonymous') and the detail page.
bugs.evidence: apps/web/src/app/(dashboard)/dashboard/people/[userId]/page.tsx:48 (redundant ternary); apps/web/src/app/(dashboard)/dashboard/people/page.tsx:84,164 ('Anonymous' label mismatch).

bugs.title: Mock fallback for People/Admin returns empty arrays, so a backend outage looks identical to genuine 'no data'
bugs.module: lib/data/fetchers.ts (fetchUserProfileSummaries, fetchAppUsers, fetchOrgPulse, etc.) + People empty states
bugs.steps: 1. Cause a backend error (e.g. Supabase unreachable / RLS denial). 2. Open /dashboard/people.

findings.summary: Audited the Integration & API surface: POST /api/v1/events ingestion (route.ts + lib/api/handler.ts, response.ts, auth.ts, rate-limit.ts, validate.ts, errors.ts, hash.ts), the public/ncpl.js auto-capture SDK against lib/schemas/events.ts, CORS config (next.config.ts + route OPTIONS), lib/supabase/* clients, repositories/events.ts (resolveUserIds/insertEventsBatch/ensureSessionsForBatch), the admin cron routes and analytics read routes, plus supabase/migrations 0002/0005/0017 for the underlying contract. The response envelope, request-id tracing, error taxonomy, and CORS preflight handling are well built. However there are several genuine contract and resilience defects: (1) the documented idempotency-via-client-`id` is broken — the insert uses plain `.insert` (a retried batch with the same id throws 500 and the SDK never sends an id anyway); (2) batch validation is all-or-nothing so one malformed event (e.g. an arbitrary `data-ncpl-event` value or a future occurredAt) rejects the whole batch; (3) the ncpl.js payload can produce values the Zod schema rejects (explicit click event names, referrer URLs); (4) the events insert is non-transactional across users→sessions→events so partial Supabase failure leaves orphaned rows; (5) the maxBytes guard trusts the spoofable/absent content-length header; (6) a per-IP in-memory rate limiter is ineffective on serverless and the bucket Map grows unbounded. Most findings are code-grounded; live HTTP behaviors are marked Needs-runtime. Verdict: functional happy path is solid, but the ingestion contract has correctness and robustness gaps that will surface in production retries, SPA edge cases, and partial-outage scenarios.

bugs.title: Idempotency contract is broken: client-supplied event id uses plain INSERT, retries 500 and the SDK never sends id
bugs.steps: 1. POST /api/v1/events with an event whose `id` is a UUID (schema trackEventSchema.id is documented 'client-supplied for idempotent retries'). 2. The same request is retried (network timeout, SDK retry, at-least-once delivery) with the same id within the same occurred_at month.
bugs.expected: Per the schema comment and migration 0002 ('event ingestion accepts client-supplied UUIDs for idempotent retries'), a retried event with the same id should be deduped (upsert / ignore-duplicates), returning success without creating a duplicate.
bugs.actual: insertEventsBatch calls `.insert(rows, { count: 'exact' })` with NO onConflict/upsert. analytics_events PK is (id, occurred_at). A duplicate id+occurred_at violates the PK, the insert returns an error, and the handler throws AppError('INGEST_FAILED', 500) — failing the ENTIRE batch, not deduping. Separately, public/ncpl.js's enqueue() never sets `ev.id`, so the idempotency key is never actually exercised by the first-party SDK at all — the only documented dedup path is dead code in practice.
bugs.fix: Use `.upsert(rows, { onConflict: 'id,occurred_at', ignoreDuplicates: true })` for the event insert so retries are idempotent, and have ncpl.js mint and send `ev.id = uuid()` per event so the dedup key exists end-to-end. Note `count` after ignoreDuplicates will not equal rows.length, so adjust the `inserted` reporting.
bugs.evidence: events.ts L150-157 plain `.insert` then `throw new AppError('INGEST_FAILED', ...)`; schema events.ts L34 `id: z.string().uuid().optional(), // client-supplied for idempotent retries`; ncpl.js L157-178 enqueue() builds `ev` with no `id` field; 0002_core_schema.sql `primary key (id, occurred_at)`.

bugs.title: Batch validation is all-or-nothing: one invalid event rejects the entire batch with 400
bugs.steps: 1. A portal emits a batch where 19 events are valid and 1 is invalid — e.g. a click on an element with `data-ncpl-event="Add To Cart!"` (contains space + '!'), or an event whose occurredAt is malformed, or a sessionId that is not a UUID. 2. ncpl.js batches up to 20 events and POSTs `{ events: batch }`.
bugs.expected: Ingestion should be resilient: valid events are accepted and only the malformed ones are dropped/reported, so a single bad event never causes data loss for the whole batch.
bugs.actual: trackEventBatchSchema validates the whole array; safeParse fails on the first invalid element and parseBody throws ValidationError (400) for the entire request. ncpl.js's flush() fire-and-forgets and swallows the rejection ('never break the host app'), so all 20 events — including the 19 valid ones — are silently lost with no retry.
bugs.fix: Parse events individually (e.g. iterate and collect valid rows + a list of rejected indices), insert the valid ones, and return 200 with `{ inserted, rejected: [...] }`. Reserve 400 for a structurally invalid body (not an array, empty, over batch cap).
bugs.evidence: validate.ts L27-31 single safeParse over whole body; events.ts L57-61 batch schema; ncpl.js L143-155 flush() with `['catch'](function(){})` swallow and no requeue.

bugs.title: ncpl.js can emit payloads the server Zod schema rejects (explicit event names, referrer, occurredAt drift)
bugs.steps: 1. Add `data-ncpl-event="Checkout Step 2"` to a button and click it → ncpl.js enqueues name='Checkout Step 2'. 2. Or land on a page whose document.referrer is a non-URL/opaque value. 3. POST batch.
bugs.expected: Every event the first-party SDK can produce should satisfy the canonical schema (the schema file states it is 'the SINGLE source of truth — both the API route and the SDK import from here').
bugs.actual: The name regex is `/^[a-z0-9._-]+$/i` (no spaces). ncpl.js passes the raw `data-ncpl-event` attribute as the event name (L253-254) with no sanitization, so 'Checkout Step 2' fails validation and (per the all-or-nothing bug above) drops the batch. referrer is validated only as `z.string().max(2048)` so that one is tolerant, but ncpl.js does not import the schema at all (it is hand-rolled vanilla JS), so the 'single source of truth' guarantee does not actually hold for the auto-capture script — drift is undetected. occurredAt is client-clock-derived (new Date().toISOString()); a skewed client clock can place events outside any existing monthly partition (only current+2 months are pre-created), landing them in analytics_events_default.
bugs.fix: Sanitize/slugify event names in ncpl.js before enqueue (lowercase, replace invalid chars), or relax the name regex. Add a server-side clamp on occurredAt (reject/clamp timestamps too far in the future/past). Add a contract test that feeds representative ncpl.js payloads through trackEventSchema in CI.
bugs.evidence: schema events.ts L37-41 name regex; ncpl.js L253-254 `enqueue('interaction', explicit, ...)` passes raw attribute; ncpl.js L170 `occurredAt: new Date().toISOString()`; ncpl.js has no import of lib/schemas; 0002 only seeds y2026m05..m07 partitions.

bugs.title: Ingestion is non-transactional: partial Supabase failure across users→sessions→events leaves orphaned/inconsistent rows
bugs.steps: 1. POST a batch. 2. resolveUserIds upserts users (best-effort, swallows errors → returns null ids), ensureSessionsForBatch upserts sessions, insertEventsBatch inserts events — three separate round-trips with no DB transaction. 3. Supabase fails between step 2 and step 3 (or the function times out mid-way).
bugs.expected: Either the whole batch lands or none of it does; sessions/users should not be created for events that never persist.
bugs.actual: The three writes are independent. If resolveUserIds partially fails it silently resolves users to null (events.ts L78-80 just console.warn), so events insert with user_id=null even though the user had an email/uuid — silent attribution loss. If ensureSessionsForBatch succeeds but insertEventsBatch throws, a session row exists with event_count still 0 and no events. There is no rollback and no compensating cleanup.
bugs.fix: Wrap the user/session/event writes in a single Postgres function (RPC) that runs in one transaction, or at minimum make resolveUserIds failures fail the request (return 503) rather than silently degrading attribution. Surface a partial-success indicator in the response.
bugs.evidence: route.ts L58-60 three sequential awaited calls; events.ts L78-80 and L107-109 swallow errors and fall through to null resolution; insertEventsBatch L154-157 throws after sessions already upserted.

bugs.title: Body-size guard trusts the Content-Length header, which is spoofable/absent (chunked uploads bypass the cap)
bugs.steps: 1. POST /api/v1/events with Transfer-Encoding: chunked (no Content-Length) or a falsified small Content-Length but a multi-MB body. 2. parseBody checks `Number(req.headers.get('content-length') ?? '0')` against maxBytes.
bugs.expected: The 64KB maxBodyBytes cap should bound actual memory consumed by req.json() regardless of declared headers.
bugs.actual: When content-length is missing it defaults to '0' (passes the check), and a lying small content-length also passes; the code then calls `await req.json()` which buffers the full real body before any size enforcement. The declared-size check is advisory only and does not protect against oversized/streamed payloads — a DoS/memory vector on the highest-traffic endpoint.
bugs.fix: Enforce the limit on the actual bytes read (e.g. read the body via a length-capped stream/reader and abort past maxBytes) rather than trusting the header. Also configure platform-level body limits.
bugs.evidence: validate.ts L15-20 only inspects the content-length header then L23 `await req.json()` with no real byte cap; RUNTIME.ingest.maxBodyBytes = 64*1024 (runtime.ts L10).

bugs.title: In-memory per-IP rate limiter is ineffective on serverless and leaks memory (unbounded bucket Map)
bugs.steps: 1. Deploy to Vercel (serverless/lambda, multiple instances, cold starts). 2. Drive traffic from many IPs over time.
bugs.expected: Rate limiting should bound request rate per client reliably, and limiter state should not grow without bound.
bugs.actual: buckets is a module-level Map in process memory. On serverless each instance has its own Map, so the 100/s burst is per-instance, not global — N instances allow N×100/s, and cold starts reset state. The Map is never pruned (no TTL/eviction), so every distinct clientIp (including spoofed x-forwarded-for values, since clientIp blindly takes the first XFF token) accumulates a Bucket entry forever — a slow memory leak and an XFF-spoofing bypass (each fake IP gets a fresh full bucket). The code comment acknowledges 'per-instance' but the configured 100/s burst gives a false sense of protection.
bugs.fix: Back the limiter with a shared store (Upstash/Redis) for real cross-instance limits, add TTL-based eviction to the Map for the fallback, and trust only the right-most XFF hop behind a known proxy (or use a platform-provided client IP).
bugs.evidence: rate-limit.ts L10 module-level Map with no eviction; L26-45 token bucket keyed by clientIp; L47-53 clientIp takes `fwd.split(',')[0]` (left-most, spoofable); route.ts L42-45 burst=100 sustained=50.

bugs.title: CORS allows wildcard origin with custom api-key header — any website can drive ingestion using a leaked public key
bugs.steps: 1. From any browser origin, send the OPTIONS preflight then POST to /api/v1/events with a valid x-ncpl-api-key. 2. Observe Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * and Allow-Headers including x-ncpl-api-key.
bugs.expected: Because the ingest key is a 'public ingest key' shipped in ncpl.js (data-key in plain HTML), CORS plus key alone cannot prevent abuse; but the platform should at least not advertise an open wildcard for an authenticated, write, cross-origin endpoint, and should bound which origins/projects can post.
bugs.actual: Both next.config.ts (L33-39) and the route's CORS_HEADERS (route.ts L20-25) set Access-Control-Allow-Origin '*' and allow the x-ncpl-api-key header for a POST that writes to the DB. Since the per-project api_key is publicly visible in the SDK script tag, any third-party site can replay it to inject arbitrary events for that project (the schema permits arbitrary metadata, names, userEmail). There is no origin allow-list and no Origin/Referer check. The config comments admit this is intended to be locked down 'once known' but it ships open.
bugs.fix: Maintain a per-project allowed-origins list (analytics_projects column), reflect the request Origin only when it matches (not '*'), and validate Origin/Referer server-side. Consider signed/short-lived ingest tokens for browser SDK rather than a static public key.
bugs.evidence: next.config.ts L33-39 ACAO '*'; route.ts L20-25 CORS_HEADERS ACAO '*' with x-ncpl-api-key allowed; ncpl.js L19 'data-key (required) public ingest key'; auth.ts L46-52 accepts any analytics_projects.api_key.

bugs.title: Auth dev soft-fail accepts ANY api key when INGEST_API_KEY is unset — open ingestion if env is missing in a real deploy
bugs.steps: 1. Deploy/run with INGEST_API_KEY unset (it is `.optional()` in env.ts). 2. POST /api/v1/events with any non-empty x-ncpl-api-key (e.g. 'x').
bugs.expected: Missing the global key should not silently disable per-project verification; an unrecognized key should be rejected outside local dev.
bugs.actual: auth.ts L42 `if (!env.INGEST_API_KEY) return;` accepts any present key without the per-project DB lookup. INGEST_API_KEY is optional in env.ts (L16), so a production deploy that forgets to set it turns ingestion into an open, unauthenticated write endpoint (any header value passes). There is no NODE_ENV guard around this soft-fail.
bugs.fix: Gate the soft-fail behind `env.NODE_ENV !== 'production'`; in production require either INGEST_API_KEY or a successful per-project key match, and fail closed otherwise.
bugs.evidence: auth.ts L41-42 unconditional `if (!env.INGEST_API_KEY) return;`; env.ts L16 `INGEST_API_KEY: z.string().min(16).optional()`.

bugs.title: Supabase-down behavior on ingest is inconsistent: users degrade silently to null but a session/event failure returns 500 with raw DB message
bugs.steps: 1. Make Supabase unreachable. 2. POST /api/v1/events with events that include sessionId and userEmail.
bugs.expected: On a backend outage the endpoint should fail fast with a stable 503/INGEST_FAILED envelope and not leak internal error strings; partial degradation should be consistent.
bugs.actual: resolveUserIds catches DB errors and resolves users to null (silent attribution loss, returns as if fine), but ensureSessionsForBatch/insertEventsBatch throw AppError with status 500 and embed the raw Supabase error.message in the client-facing envelope (events.ts L155, L190). So the same outage yields either silent data corruption (user_id lost) or a 500 leaking `error.message` — inconsistent and leaky. A DB outage should arguably be 503 (retryable) not 500.
bugs.fix: Return a generic INGEST_FAILED message (log details server-side only), use 503 for upstream unavailability so clients retry, and treat resolveUserIds failure the same way as session/event failure rather than silently nulling.
bugs.evidence: events.ts L78-80/L107-109 swallow + null; L155 `\`Event insert failed: ${error.message}\``; L190 `error.message`; handler.ts only sanitizes truly-unknown errors (L51-55), AppError messages pass through verbatim (L47).

bugs.title: Dead/duplicate body-size constants and SDK/server batch-cap mismatch create contract confusion
bugs.module: apps/web/src/constants/api.ts vs apps/web/src/config/runtime.ts vs public/ncpl.js vs lib/schemas/events.ts
bugs.steps: Static review of the configured limits.
bugs.expected: A single authoritative body-size and batch-size limit used consistently by SDK and server.
bugs.actual: constants/api.ts defines MAX_EVENT_PAYLOAD_BYTES = 32*1024 (32KB) but the events route enforces RUNTIME.ingest.maxBodyBytes = 64*1024 (64KB) — the 32KB constant is never used by the route, so docs/SDK relying on it under-estimate. MAX_EVENT_BATCH_SIZE=50 (server cap) while ncpl.js MAX_BATCH=20 (fine), but there is no shared constant — drift is possible. These inconsistencies make the published request contract ambiguous.
bugs.fix: Delete or reconcile MAX_EVENT_PAYLOAD_BYTES to match RUNTIME.ingest.maxBodyBytes, and document the authoritative batch + byte limits in one place that both SDK and route reference.
bugs.evidence: constants/api.ts L15-16 (MAX_EVENT_BATCH_SIZE=50, MAX_EVENT_PAYLOAD_BYTES=32KB, unused by route); runtime.ts L10 maxBodyBytes=64KB used in route.ts L49; ncpl.js L135 MAX_BATCH=20.

recommendations: Make ingestion idempotent end-to-end: switch insertEventsBatch to upsert with onConflict 'id,occurred_at' ignoreDuplicates, and have ncpl.js mint+send a per-event UUID (ev.id) so the documented retry-dedup actually works.

Change batch handling from all-or-nothing to partial-success: validate each event independently, insert the valid subset, and return { inserted, rejected } so a single malformed event never drops a whole batch (which the SDK silently discards).

Add a CI contract test that runs representative public/ncpl.js payloads (auto page_view, route_change, interaction.click, explicit data-ncpl-event names, error.captured, performance.*) through trackEventSchema to catch SDK↔schema drift; sanitize/slugify event names in ncpl.js before enqueue.
Fail closed on auth in production: gate the `INGEST_API_KEY` unset soft-fail behind NODE_ENV !== 'production', and consider making INGEST_API_KEY required when no per-project keys are provisioned.

Enforce the 64KB body cap on actual bytes read (length-capped stream) rather than the spoofable/absent Content-Length header; reconcile/remove the unused 32KB MAX_EVENT_PAYLOAD_BYTES constant so the published byte limit is unambiguous.

Replace the in-memory token-bucket with a shared store (e.g. Upstash/Redis) for real cross-instance limits, add TTL eviction to prevent unbounded Map growth, and stop trusting the left-most x-forwarded-for hop for the bucket key.
Lock CORS to a per-project allowed-origins list (reflect matching Origin instead of '*') and validate Origin/Referer server-side, since the browser ingest key is public by design.

Make ingestion atomic and consistent on partial failure: wrap users→sessions→events in a single transactional RPC, treat resolveUserIds failure as a request failure (avoid silent user_id=null attribution loss), return 503 (retryable) for upstream DB outages, and never echo raw Supabase error.message to clients.
Clamp/validate occurredAt server-side (reject timestamps far outside the partition window) so client clock skew doesn't dump events into analytics_events_default.

findings.summary: Audited performance & large-data handling across the analytics repositories (analytics.ts, journeys.ts, operational.ts), the SQL views/materialized views in supabase/migrations (0002, 0003, 0017, 0019, 0020), the MV refresh cron wiring (vercel.json + admin routes), and the force-dynamic dashboard pages that consume them. Verdict: NOT READY for 10k+ scale. The architecture is built on the right primitives (partitioned analytics_events, good covering indexes, three MVs, a cron) but the wiring has a fatal defect and the hot read paths bypass the MVs in favor of JS-side aggregation over capped/unbounded row pulls. The single most severe issue: Vercel Cron issues GET requests but both maintenance routes (refresh-aggregates, ensure-partitions) export only POST, so materialized views are NEVER refreshed and new month partitions are NEVER created in production. On top of that, the only MV actually read by code is mv_portal_daily; the other two MVs the cron refreshes (mv_user_daily, mv_feature_usage_30d) are typed in database.ts but never queried, while the high-traffic getActiveUsers / getJourneyGraph / cross-app People views all aggregate in JS over raw events. At 10k+ events these queries pull tens of thousands of rows per page render (each page is force-dynamic, no caching), and getActiveUsers silently produces WRONG results because of a 10000-row LIMIT applied before aggregation.

bugs.title: Vercel Cron (GET) never triggers MV refresh or partition creation — handlers only export POST
bugs.steps: 1. Deploy to Vercel. 2. vercel.json schedules cron hits to /api/v1/admin/refresh-aggregates (*/5) and /api/v1/admin/ensure-partitions (monthly). 3. Vercel Cron invokes these paths with an HTTP GET. 4. Both route files export only `export const POST = ...` — there is no GET export.
bugs.expected: Cron invocation runs refresh_analytics_aggregates() every 5 min and ensure_events_partition() monthly.
bugs.actual: GET requests hit a route with no GET handler → 405 Method Not Allowed. refresh_analytics_aggregates() is never called, so mv_portal_daily / mv_user_daily / mv_feature_usage_30d stay frozen at whatever data they last had (they are created `with no data`, so they may be permanently EMPTY). ensure_events_partition() never runs, so once the seeded partitions (2026-05/06/07) lapse, new events fall into analytics_events_default and partition pruning stops helping.
bugs.fix: Add `export const GET = POST;` (or rename to GET) in both route files — Vercel Cron sends GET. Keep CRON_SECRET via the Authorization: Bearer header (requireCronSecret already reads `authorization`). Verify mv_portal_daily is populated after first refresh; consider an initial `refresh materialized view` in a migration so they aren't empty on day one.
bugs.evidence: vercel.json lines 7-16 schedule both paths. refresh-aggregates/route.ts line 16 `export const POST = withApiHandler(...)` with no GET. ensure-partitions/route.ts line 18 same. Vercel Cron documented behavior is GET. mv definitions in 0003_aggregations.sql lines 38/56/74 all end `with no data`, so without a successful refresh they return zero rows.

bugs.title: getActiveUsers returns WRONG top-users ranking due to 10000-row LIMIT applied before JS aggregation
bugs.steps: 1. Have >10000 events in the trailing 30 days (trivial at 10k+ scale). 2. Open /dashboard/users (fetchActiveUsers → getActiveUsers). 3. Query selects user_id+occurred_at ordered by occurred_at DESC limited to 10000, then counts per user in JS.
bugs.expected: Top N users by 30-day event count.
bugs.actual: The .limit(10000) takes only the 10000 most RECENT events, then counts within that window. A user who was very active 20 days ago but quiet recently is undercounted or missing entirely; the 'top by events' ranking reflects only the most recent slice, not the 30-day total. Counts shown in events24h are systematically wrong/under-reported once daily volume exceeds ~10000/30. The result is silently incorrect with no error.
bugs.fix: Aggregate in SQL, not JS: either query mv_user_daily (sum events over last 30 days, order desc, limit N) — that MV exists for exactly this — or add a Postgres RPC `select user_id, count(*) ... group by user_id order by count desc limit N`. Both return the true top-N in one cheap indexed pass and transfer N rows instead of 10000.
bugs.evidence: analytics.ts lines 212-238: select ... order('occurred_at', desc).limit(10000) then `for (const r of rows) agg...` then sort by events desc slice(0,limit). The LIMIT-then-aggregate ordering is the bug. mv_user_daily (0003 lines 56-69) already pre-aggregates per (user_id, day) and is unused by any code.

bugs.title: getJourneyGraph pulls up to 20000 raw page_view rows and builds Sankey in JS — unbounded by session, truncates at scale
bugs.steps: 1. Accumulate >20000 navigation.page_view events in 30 days. 2. Open /dashboard/journeys (force-dynamic). 3. Query .eq('name','navigation.page_view').gte(30d).order(occurred_at asc).limit(20000).
bugs.expected: Journey flow reflecting all sessions in the window.
bugs.actual: Two problems: (a) the .limit(20000) with order ASC keeps only the OLDEST 20000 page-views, so recent journeys are dropped and the diagram is stale/partial once volume exceeds the cap; (b) 20000 rows incl. jsonb metadata are shipped to Node and grouped per session in JS on every page load. No SQL aggregation, no cache. At high volume this is a large transfer + GC churn on each render.
bugs.fix: Push the sessionize+transition counting into SQL (a view or RPC using window functions / lag() over partition by session_id order by occurred_at) returning already-aggregated (fromStep, from, to, count) rows. Cap per-session steps in SQL. If keeping JS, at minimum order DESC and bound by session count, and add caching/revalidate so it doesn't recompute on every hit.
bugs.evidence: journeys.ts lines 92-99 select session_id, occurred_at, metadata ... order asc .limit(20000); lines 105-125 build bySession map and transition map entirely in JS. metadata is jsonb (0002 line 111), so each row carries a JSON blob.

bugs.title: Every dashboard page is force-dynamic with no caching — heavy live aggregations re-run on each request
bugs.steps: 1. Any dashboard route loads. 2. force-dynamic disables Full Route Cache and revalidation. 3. The page re-executes its fetchers (each a live Supabase aggregation) on every request, every refresh, every user.
bugs.expected: Aggregations refreshed on a sensible cadence (the MVs already imply a 5-min freshness target) and cached between requests.
bugs.actual: No `revalidate` is set anywhere; every page is fully dynamic. Pages like /dashboard (7 parallel fetchers incl. getOrgPulse/getEventsTimeSeries which scan 24h–30d of events) and /dashboard/journeys (20000-row pull) recompute from raw events on each load. Under concurrent admins this multiplies DB load and TTFB. The MV/cron design intended cached rollups, but the read paths bypass them.
bugs.fix: Add `export const revalidate = 300;` (match the 5-min cron) to read-only dashboard pages, or use unstable_cache around fetchers. Route the heavy reads (active users, journeys, category breakdown, time series) through the materialized views so even on a cold render they hit pre-aggregated rows.
bugs.evidence: grep of page.tsx files: all 16 dashboard pages export dynamic='force-dynamic'; none export revalidate. dashboard/page.tsx line 46 Promise.all of 7 live fetchers.

bugs.title: Cross-app People views (v_user_app_profile / v_user_profile_summary) aggregate over the ENTIRE analytics_events history with no time bound
bugs.steps: 1. analytics_events grows to 10k+/large history. 2. Open /dashboard/people (getUserProfileSummaries) or a per-app view (getAppUsers) or a person page (getUserDetail joins v_user_app_profile). 3. Views join analytics_users to analytics_events and GROUP BY with no occurred_at filter.
bugs.expected: People metrics computed over a bounded, indexed window.
bugs.actual: v_user_app_profile and v_user_profile_summary scan the full analytics_events table (all partitions) every time, grouping by user. There is no WHERE occurred_at >= ... so partition pruning cannot help and the cost grows unbounded with total history. The `.limit(200)` in the page only limits returned rows AFTER the full aggregation+sort runs. getUserDetail also derives totalEvents by summing v_user_app_profile (full-history) instead of the recent window.
bugs.fix: Add a rolling time window to the people views (e.g. occurred_at >= now() - interval '90 days') or back them with mv_user_daily. Add a composite index supporting (user_id, occurred_at) — analytics_events_user_occurred_idx exists, but the view still aggregates all-time. Consider materializing v_user_profile_summary.
bugs.evidence: 0020 lines 96-99 (v_user_app_profile) join with no time predicate, group by u.id...e.portal_id. lines 115-118 (v_user_profile_summary) left join with no time predicate. operational.ts getAppUsers line 56-62 selects from the view then .limit(limit) (post-aggregation). getUserDetail line 179 sums apps[].events from the full-history view.

bugs.title: getOrgPulse appsActive computed in JS over a 10000-row pull instead of count(distinct portal_id)
bugs.steps: 1. >10000 events today. 2. Load /dashboard (fetchOrgPulse). 3. Query select('portal_id').gte(today).limit(10000) then new Set(...).size in JS.
bugs.expected: Distinct active app count for today.
bugs.actual: If today's events exceed 10000, only the first 10000 (no explicit order, so arbitrary/insertion order) are fetched; distinct portal_id is computed over that partial slice. The active-apps figure can be understated, and 10000 rows are transferred just to count distinct of a tiny enum. Correctness degrades at scale and the transfer is wasteful.
bugs.fix: Replace with a SQL distinct count: an RPC or view `select count(distinct portal_id) from analytics_events where occurred_at >= today`. portal_id is a low-cardinality enum, so this is trivially cheap and exact.
bugs.evidence: operational.ts lines 27, 32-34: admin.from('analytics_events').select('portal_id').gte('occurred_at', since).limit(10000), then `new Set(((activeRes.data ?? [])...).map(r=>r.portal_id)).size`.

bugs.title: getPortalSummaries and getEventsTimeSeries/getCategoryBreakdown fall back to / use unbounded 24h row pulls aggregated in JS
bugs.steps: 1. mv_portal_daily empty (which it is, per the broken cron) OR these other functions called. 2. getPortalSummaries falls back to selecting ALL 24h events (portal_id,user_id,session_id,category) with no limit and aggregates in JS. getEventsTimeSeries selects ALL 24h (occurred_at,user_id) ordered, buckets in JS. getCategoryBreakdown selects ALL 24h categories.
bugs.expected: Bounded, indexed aggregation (ideally via MV or SQL group by).
bugs.actual: Given the cron defect, mv_portal_daily is empty, so getPortalSummaries always takes the fallback branch that pulls every event in the last 24h into Node. getEventsTimeSeries and getCategoryBreakdown have NO row limit at all — they stream the entire 24h of events to the server for JS counting. At 10k+ events/day these are large unbounded transfers on every (force-dynamic) render of the home dashboard.
bugs.fix: Implement SQL GROUP BY (RPC/view) for category breakdown, hourly time series (date_trunc('hour', occurred_at)), and portal summary; or rely on mv_portal_daily once the cron is fixed. Never select unbounded event sets for client-side counting.
bugs.evidence: analytics.ts getPortalSummaries fallback lines 74-92 (no .limit), getEventsTimeSeries lines 141-145 (no .limit, full 24h), getCategoryBreakdown lines 182-185 (no .limit). The MV-first branch (lines 57-71) is dead in production because the refresh cron never runs.

bugs.title: refresh_analytics_aggregates uses REFRESH CONCURRENTLY on MVs that may be empty (with no data) — first refresh can error
bugs.steps: 1. MVs are created `with no data` (never populated). 2. First call to refresh_analytics_aggregates runs `refresh materialized view CONCURRENTLY`.
bugs.expected: Refresh succeeds.
bugs.actual: Postgres does not allow REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW CONCURRENTLY on a view that has never been populated with data (the first refresh must be non-concurrent). So even if the cron route is fixed to GET, the very first refresh will fail with 'CONCURRENTLY cannot be used when the materialized view is not populated', and mv_* stay empty until someone runs a plain refresh manually.
bugs.fix: Either create the MVs WITH DATA, or do an initial non-concurrent `refresh materialized view public.mv_*` in a migration, or make refresh_analytics_aggregates detect an unpopulated MV (pg_class.relispopulated) and do the first refresh non-concurrently.
bugs.evidence: 0003 lines 38/56/74 `with no data`; lines 98-100 `refresh materialized view concurrently`. This is a documented Postgres restriction.

bugs.title: getUserDetail pulls up to 2000 sessions and sums durations in JS per profile view
bugs.steps: 1. A heavy user with many sessions. 2. Open /dashboard/people/[userId]. 3. Query analytics_sessions for the user .limit(2000), then loop in JS computing totalMs.
bugs.expected: Total session minutes computed in SQL.
bugs.actual: Caps at 2000 sessions (silently undercounts a very active user) and transfers up to 2000 rows to sum durations in JS. Cheap-ish per request but unnecessary; the sum belongs in SQL. Combined with force-dynamic, recomputed every view.
bugs.fix: Compute sum(extract(epoch from coalesce(ended_at,last_seen_at)-started_at)) and count(*) in a single SQL aggregate keyed by user_id; drop the 2000 cap.
bugs.evidence: operational.ts line 146 .limit(2000); lines 163-169 JS loop summing end-start.

testCases.scenario: MV refresh cron actually fires in production
testCases.steps: Deploy; let Vercel Cron hit /api/v1/admin/refresh-aggregates; inspect response status and whether mv_portal_daily has rows for today.
testCases.expected: 200 OK and mv_portal_daily populated.

testCases.scenario: getActiveUsers correctness above the 10000-row cap
testCases.steps: Seed 30 days with one user having 5000 events 25 days ago and others with fewer recent events such that total events in 30d > 10000; call getActiveUsers(50); compare ranking against a SQL group-by-count baseline.
testCases.expected: Top-N ranking matches the true 30-day per-user counts.

testCases.scenario: Journey graph completeness above 20000 page_views
testCases.steps: Seed >20000 navigation.page_view events spanning 30 days; render /dashboard/journeys; verify recent sessions are represented.
testCases.expected: Diagram reflects full window (or a clearly documented recent window), not just the oldest 20000 rows.

testCases.steps: Load test /dashboard with ~50k events in 24h; measure DB rows transferred and p95 TTFB across repeated loads.
testCases.expected: Bounded row transfer (MV-backed) and stable TTFB across loads.

testCases.steps: On a fresh DB (MVs unpopulated), call SELECT refresh_analytics_aggregates();
testCases.expected: Succeeds and populates all three MVs.

testCases.steps: Advance to after 2026-07; confirm ensure-partitions cron created analytics_events_y2026m08 and that new events are NOT landing in analytics_events_default.
testCases.expected: New monthly partition exists; default partition stays empty.

testCases.expected: Plan uses bounded window / index, not a full all-partition seq-scan aggregation.

recommendations: Fix the cron immediately: export GET (aliased to the POST logic) in both /api/v1/admin/refresh-aggregates and /api/v1/admin/ensure-partitions, since Vercel Cron issues GET. Add a smoke test asserting GET returns 200 with the CRON_SECRET bearer header. This single fix is prerequisite to any MV-based scaling.

Move client-side (JS) aggregation into SQL. Replace getActiveUsers, getOrgPulse appsActive, getCategoryBreakdown, getEventsTimeSeries, and the journey sessionization with SQL GROUP BY / window-function RPCs or materialized views. JS aggregation over capped/unbounded row pulls is the root cause of both the correctness bugs and the scaling cost.

Actually use the materialized views you already build. mv_user_daily and mv_feature_usage_30d are refreshed (once cron is fixed) but never read; route getActiveUsers through mv_user_daily and feature reads through mv_feature_usage_30d. Route getPortalSummaries/time-series through mv_portal_daily.

Remove the silent LIMIT-then-aggregate anti-pattern everywhere (10000 in getActiveUsers/getOrgPulse, 20000 in getJourneyGraph, 2000 sessions in getUserDetail). Any cap applied before aggregation yields wrong totals with no error — either aggregate in SQL (no cap needed) or apply LIMIT only to already-aggregated output.

Add caching to the read-only dashboards: set `export const revalidate = 300` (aligned with the 5-min MV cadence) or wrap fetchers in unstable_cache, instead of blanket force-dynamic, so heavy aggregations are not recomputed on every request and every concurrent admin.
Bound the People views (v_user_app_profile, v_user_profile_summary, v_inactive_users) with a rolling time window or materialize them; they currently aggregate the entire event history per page load.

Make the first MV refresh non-concurrent (or create the MVs WITH DATA) so refresh_analytics_aggregates doesn't fail on an unpopulated view; have refresh_analytics_aggregates check pg_class.relispopulated and pick CONCURRENTLY vs plain accordingly.

Add monitoring/alerting on MV staleness and on the default partition row count (alert if analytics_events_default is non-empty) so the GET/POST class of failure is caught in production rather than silently degrading dashboards to mock fallback or stale data.

findings.summary: Static security audit (OWASP-oriented) of the NCPL analytics platform (Next.js 15 App Router + Supabase, apps/web). I read middleware.ts, lib/supabase/middleware.ts + admin.ts, lib/api/auth.ts, all (dashboard) pages + layout, lib/data/fetchers.ts, every repository, lib/schemas/events.ts, lib/api/{rate-limit,validate,handler}.ts, lib/env.ts, public/ncpl.js, next.config.ts, the admin server action, the analytics/admin API routes, and supabase/migrations/0002_core_schema.sql (RLS). VERDICT: NOT SAFE TO DEPLOY PUBLICLY. The headline issue confirmed from the task brief is real and severe: dashboard PAGES are completely unauthenticated. middleware.ts only refreshes the Supabase session and explicitly "does not gate any routes"; no (dashboard) page or layout calls requireAdmin/getUser/redirect; and the pages render via lib/data/fetchers.ts which call repositories that use the service-role admin client (lib/supabase/admin.ts) directly, bypassing RLS. There is no login page anywhere. Net effect: any unauthenticated visitor to the deployed URL reads ALL analytics — every user's email, name, department, per-person activity timeline, logins, sessions, and cross-app behavior. The hardened API routes that DO call requireAdmin (e.g. /api/v1/analytics/dashboard) are dead weight because the UI never uses them. Secondary issues: an unauthenticated server action that creates projects and mints ingest keys; ingest key design that lets any valid key spoof any portalId; a dev soft-fail that accepts ANY key when INGEST_API_KEY is unset; per-instance in-memory rate limiting; a default IP-hash salt; CORS '*' on ingestion; and a content-length-only body size guard. Positives: repositories use the Supabase query builder (parameterized) — no raw SQL string interpolation, so SQL injection is not present; React auto-escapes all rendered event/user fields — no dangerouslySetInnerHTML in ActivityFeed/people pages, so stored XSS via event name/metadata is not present; Zod schemas are strict() and validate ingest input well; safeEqual is constant-time-ish for key checks.

bugs.title: Dashboard pages are completely unauthenticated — anyone can read all analytics and PII
bugs.steps: 1. Deploy the app. 2. As an unauthenticated visitor (no cookie/session), navigate directly to https://<host>/dashboard, /dashboard/people, /dashboard/people/<userId>, /dashboard/portals, /dashboard/realtime, /dashboard/reliability, etc. 3. Observe full data renders. middleware.ts (lines 4-11) only calls updateSession which 'does not gate any routes' (lib/supabase/middleware.ts line 9 + comment); it never inspects auth.getUser() result nor redirects. No (dashboard) page or layout.tsx calls requireAdmin/getUser/redirect (grep for requireAdmin|getSupabaseServer|auth.getUser|redirect across (dashboard) returns ZERO matches). Each page (e.g. dashboard/page.tsx lines 45-54, people/page.tsx lines 17-35) awaits fetchers which call repositories that use getSupabaseAdmin() (service-role, RLS-bypassing).
bugs.expected: Unauthenticated requests to /dashboard/* should redirect to a login page (which does not exist) or return 401/403. Server components should call requireAdmin() (as the API routes do) before fetching, or middleware should gate the (dashboard) segment.
bugs.actual: All dashboard pages render fully for anonymous visitors. People pages expose every user's email, display name, department, team, title, login counts, session minutes, per-app activity, and a recent-activity timeline (operational.ts getUserProfileSummaries/getAppUsers/getUserDetail). This is a complete authentication bypass and mass PII/data exposure (OWASP A01 Broken Access Control + A07).
bugs.fix: Gate the (dashboard) route group. Minimal: in apps/web/src/app/(dashboard)/layout.tsx make it an async server component that calls requireAdmin() (from lib/api/auth.ts) and redirect('/login') on AuthError/ForbiddenError. Better defense-in-depth: also enforce in middleware.ts — after supabase.auth.getUser(), if the path starts with /dashboard and there is no user (or is_analytics_admin is false), return NextResponse.redirect to a login route. Build the missing login page. Do NOT rely on the API routes' requireAdmin since the UI bypasses them by calling repositories directly.
bugs.evidence: apps/web/src/lib/supabase/middleware.ts line 9: 'Phase 1 does not gate any routes.' and line 34 just `await supabase.auth.getUser()` with the result discarded. apps/web/src/app/(dashboard)/layout.tsx is a plain non-async component with no auth. Grep for requireAdmin across (dashboard) = no matches. apps/web/src/lib/data/fetchers.ts imports repositories that all `import { getSupabaseAdmin }` (e.g. operational.ts line 2). Contrast: apps/web/src/app/api/v1/analytics/dashboard/route.ts line 11 DOES `await requireAdmin()`, proving the gate exists but is unused by the UI.

bugs.title: Unauthenticated server action createProjectAction creates projects and mints ingest keys
bugs.steps: 1. createProjectAction is a 'use server' action (actions.ts line 1) invoked from the unauthenticated admin page. 2. It validates the form input with Zod (lines 55-63) but performs NO authentication/authorization check before calling createProject(). 3. createProject (projects.ts lines 104-129) runs with getSupabaseAdmin() (service role), calls rpc('add_portal_value') to mutate a Postgres enum, upserts analytics_portals, and inserts analytics_projects with a freshly generated api_key (generateApiKey, line 46). 4. An attacker can POST the Next.js server-action payload directly (server actions are reachable over HTTP) to create arbitrary projects and obtain a working ingest key.
bugs.expected: The action must call requireAdmin() (or equivalent) at the top and reject unauthenticated/non-admin callers before any DB mutation.
bugs.actual: No auth gate. Anonymous callers can grow the portal_id enum (irreversible schema change in Postgres — enum values cannot be dropped), create projects, and mint valid ncpl_pk_ ingest keys, which they can then use to inject events. OWASP A01 Broken Access Control + A05 Misconfiguration.
bugs.fix: At the start of createProjectAction (after 'use server'), call `await requireAdmin()` inside the try and return { ok:false, error:'Unauthorized' } on AuthError/ForbiddenError. Since requireAdmin uses getSupabaseServer() (cookie-bound) it works inside server actions. Also gate the admin page itself.
bugs.evidence: apps/web/src/app/(dashboard)/dashboard/admin/projects/actions.ts lines 39-79: createProjectAction body goes straight from Zod parse to createProject with no auth import (no requireAdmin imported in the file). projects.ts line 118 `admin.rpc('add_portal_value', { p_slug: slug })` mutates the enum; line 128 mints the key.

bugs.title: Ingest key does not bind to portalId — any valid key can spoof events for any project
bugs.steps: 1. requireIngestKey (auth.ts lines 34-58) checks the x-ncpl-api-key header against EITHER the global INGEST_API_KEY OR any per-project key where tracking_enabled=true. It returns void on success and never returns/validates WHICH project the key belongs to. 2. The events route (route.ts lines 41-65) then ingests events whose portalId comes entirely from the request body, validated only as a slug shape (events.ts portalIdSchema, lines 14-18). 3. Because ncpl.js ships data-key in plain client HTML (ncpl.js lines 9, 19, 35-36, 151 send KEY in the header), the key is public. 4. Anyone with any one valid key can POST events with portalId set to ANY other project's slug, polluting/forging another app's analytics, logins (auth.login), error rates, and user identities (userEmail).
bugs.expected: A per-project key should authorize ONLY its own portalId. requireIngestKey should return the resolved project slug and the route should reject events whose portalId != the key's project. The global shared key (if kept) is inherently spoofable and should be scoped or retired.
bugs.actual: No key↔portalId binding. Combined with the publicly-visible data-key, an attacker can spoof events for arbitrary projects, forge user identities by email, inflate/deflate metrics, and create synthetic users (events.ts resolveUserIds mints users from attacker-supplied userEmail/userName). OWASP A01/A04 (insecure design of a multi-tenant trust boundary).
bugs.fix: Make requireIngestKey return the authorized project slug (or null for the global key). In the events route, after auth, reject any event whose portalId does not match the authorized slug (400/403). Consider removing the global shared-secret path for browser-embedded keys, or restrict the global key to trusted server-to-server callers only.
bugs.evidence: auth.ts lines 46-52 select only 'slug' but discard it (returns void). route.ts line 46 `await requireIngestKey(req)` then line 48 parses events with body-supplied portalId; nothing cross-checks. ncpl.js line 151 `'x-ncpl-api-key': KEY` where KEY = data-key attribute (line 36) embedded in public HTML.

bugs.title: Ingestion dev soft-fail accepts ANY api key when INGEST_API_KEY is unset
bugs.steps: 1. INGEST_API_KEY is optional in env.ts (line 16: .optional()). 2. requireIngestKey (auth.ts line 42): `if (!env.INGEST_API_KEY) return;` — when the global key env var is absent, ANY non-empty x-ncpl-api-key header is accepted (it returns before the per-project DB lookup). 3. If the platform is deployed without INGEST_API_KEY configured (easy to forget — it is optional, not required), the ingestion endpoint authenticates every request that sends any header value.
bugs.expected: Missing ingest secret should fail closed (reject), or at minimum only behave permissively in NODE_ENV=development. Production must require a configured key.
bugs.actual: Open ingestion in any environment where INGEST_API_KEY is unset — unauthenticated event injection / data poisoning / synthetic user creation. OWASP A05 Security Misconfiguration / A07.
bugs.fix: Remove the unconditional `if (!env.INGEST_API_KEY) return;` or guard it with `if (!env.INGEST_API_KEY) { if (env.NODE_ENV !== 'production') return; throw new AuthError('Ingest not configured'); }`. Better: make INGEST_API_KEY (or per-project keys) mandatory in production by validating in env.ts when NODE_ENV==='production'.
bugs.evidence: apps/web/src/lib/api/auth.ts line 41-42: comment 'Dev soft-fail: no global key configured — accept any present key.' followed by `if (!env.INGEST_API_KEY) return;`. env.ts line 16 marks INGEST_API_KEY optional with no production enforcement.

bugs.title: Default IP-hash salt ships in code (weak pseudonymization of session IPs)
bugs.steps: 1. env.ts line 18 defaults IP_HASH_SALT to the literal 'ncpl-default-salt-change-me'. 2. clientIp/hashIp store SHA-256(salt+ip) in analytics_sessions.ip_hash and event metadata._ip_hash (events route lines 52-53; events.ts insertEventsBatch line 144). 3. If the salt is left at the default (it is optional with a default, so deployments may never set it), the IP hashes are computable/reversible by brute force over the IPv4 space using the publicly-known salt, defeating the pseudonymization.
bugs.expected: IP_HASH_SALT should have no insecure default and be required (or randomly generated per deployment); pseudonymized IPs should not be brute-forceable with a public salt.
bugs.actual: With the default salt, session IPs can be de-anonymized (rainbow/brute-force over 32-bit IPv4 space), a privacy regression. OWASP A02 Cryptographic Failures / privacy.
bugs.fix: Remove the default in env.ts (require IP_HASH_SALT, min length raised), or enforce a non-default value in production. Document rotation.
bugs.evidence: apps/web/src/lib/env.ts line 18: `IP_HASH_SALT: z.string().min(8).default('ncpl-default-salt-change-me')`. Used in events route lines 52-53 and persisted in events.ts line 144.

bugs.title: In-memory per-instance rate limiter — ineffective on serverless/multi-region and resets on cold start
bugs.steps: 1. rate-limit.ts uses a module-level Map<string,Bucket> (line 10). On Vercel/serverless each instance has its own Map, and cold starts wipe it. 2. clientIp (lines 47-53) trusts the first value of x-forwarded-for with no validation; an attacker can rotate/forge X-Forwarded-For to get a fresh bucket per request, fully bypassing the limit. 3. The events route relies solely on this limiter (route.ts lines 42-45) for abuse protection of ingestion.
bugs.expected: Rate limiting should be shared/durable (e.g. Upstash/Redis or Vercel WAF) and key on a trustworthy client identity; spoofable headers should not reset the bucket.
bugs.actual: Limiter provides little real protection: bypassable by spoofing X-Forwarded-For and non-coordinated across instances. OWASP A04 Insecure Design / lack of anti-automation. (The code comment acknowledges this — 'pair with Vercel WAF'.)
bugs.fix: Use a shared store (Redis/Upstash) or platform WAF for ingestion limits. Derive the client key from the platform-provided trusted IP (Vercel's request.ip / x-vercel-forwarded-for) rather than raw X-Forwarded-For. Treat the in-memory limiter as best-effort only.

bugs.title: Ingestion CORS allows any origin and body-size guard relies only on Content-Length
bugs.steps: 1. Access-Control-Allow-Origin is '*' for /api/v1/events (route.ts line 21-25 and next.config.ts lines 33-39) — any website can POST events from a victim's browser. Combined with the publicly-embedded data-key this widens spoofing/CSRF-style event injection. 2. parseBody enforces maxBytes only by reading the Content-Length header (validate.ts lines 15-19); a client can omit/understate it (e.g. chunked transfer) to send a larger body, which is then fully buffered by req.json(). 3. trackEventSchema.metadata is z.record(z.string(), z.unknown()) (events.ts line 51) with no per-value size or nesting limit, so within an allowed batch each event can carry large/deep JSON that lands in jsonb.
bugs.expected: CORS should be locked to known portal origins (the code comments say to). Body-size enforcement should not depend solely on a client-supplied header. Metadata should have bounded size/depth.
bugs.actual: Any-origin ingestion plus a spoofable size guard and unbounded metadata enable cross-origin abuse and memory/storage amplification. OWASP A05 Misconfiguration / A04 Insecure Design.
bugs.fix: Replace ACAO '*' with an allow-list of portal origins once known. In parseBody, also bound the actually-read bytes (e.g. read the stream with a cap) instead of trusting Content-Length. Add a max serialized-size / depth check on metadata in trackEventSchema.
