recommendations: TOP PRIORITY: Gate the entire (dashboard) route group. Make apps/web/src/app/(dashboard)/layout.tsx an async server component that calls requireAdmin() and redirect()s on failure, AND enforce in middleware.ts (inspect supabase.auth.getUser() and redirect unauthenticated /dashboard requests). Build the missing login page. Until then the platform must not be exposed publicly.

Add `await requireAdmin()` to the createProjectAction server action (and any future mutating server action) before touching the DB, and gate the admin page. Server actions are HTTP-reachable and currently mint ingest keys for anyone.

Bind ingest keys to their project: have requireIngestKey return the authorized slug and reject events whose portalId != that slug. Reconsider the browser-embedded global shared key model entirely (it is public by design in ncpl.js).

Fail closed on ingestion auth: remove/guard the `if (!env.INGEST_API_KEY) return;` soft-fail so production rejects requests when no key is configured; consider requiring INGEST_API_KEY in env.ts when NODE_ENV==='production'.
Remove the default IP_HASH_SALT and require a per-deployment random salt; document rotation. A public salt makes IP pseudonymization reversible.
Move rate limiting to a shared/durable store (Upstash/Redis) or the platform WAF and key it on a trusted client IP, not raw X-Forwarded-For. Treat the in-memory limiter as best-effort only.

Lock Access-Control-Allow-Origin for /api/v1/events to a known portal allow-list (both route.ts and next.config.ts). Enforce request body size by bytes actually read, not just Content-Length, and bound metadata size/nesting in trackEventSchema.
Add a CSP header (currently none in next.config.ts securityHeaders) to harden the dashboard against XSS even though current rendering is safe.

Add automated tests: an integration test asserting anonymous /dashboard/* returns 401/redirect, and a test asserting createProjectAction rejects unauthenticated callers — both would have caught the access-control gaps.

Positive controls to preserve: keep the requireAdmin gate on the /api/v1/analytics/* routes, the requireCronSecret gate on /api/v1/admin/*, the strict() Zod ingest schemas, the constant-time safeEqual comparisons, and the parameterized Supabase query builder usage (no raw SQL) — these are done correctly.

findings.summary: Audited role-based access across migrations (0002_core_schema.sql, 0005, 0019, 0020), the is_analytics_admin() RPC, lib/api/auth.ts (requireAdmin), middleware, the dashboard layout/pages, server actions, and the repository/data-fetcher layer. VERDICT: The spec's three-tier Admin/Manager/User model is NOT implemented. The schema defines analytics_users.role as a free-text column with values member|admin|owner, but the only distinction the code ever makes is binary: is_analytics_admin() returns true for role IN ('admin','owner') and false for everything else. There is no 'manager' role, no Manager tier anywhere in code (grep for manager/Manager finds only SDK/lock-file noise), and 'member' users have effectively zero access (RLS denies all analytics tables to non-admins). It is functionally a single admin-vs-not gate, not three roles. Worse, the enforcement that does exist is bypassed on the entire dashboard UI: requireAdmin() is only called by the 5 GET API routes under /api/v1, while every dashboard server-component page reads data through fetchers -> repositories that use the service-role admin client (getSupabaseAdmin, bypasses RLS) with NO requireAdmin() call, no middleware route gate (updateSession only refreshes the session, explicitly 'does not gate any routes'), and no auth check in (dashboard)/layout.tsx. There is also no login page in the app at all. Net result: the dashboard's RBAC is largely theoretical — the real data path neither authenticates nor authorizes. Plus a privilege-escalation gap in the RLS self-update policy. Most UI authorization checks require a live runtime to fully confirm and are marked Needs-runtime.

bugs.title: Spec's Admin/Manager/User three-tier RBAC is not implemented — only a binary admin gate exists
bugs.steps: 1. Read analytics_users.role definition (0002 line 52): values member|admin|owner. 2. Read is_analytics_admin() (0002 lines 248-254): returns true only for role IN ('admin','owner'). 3. grep -ri 'manager' across the codebase: no Manager role/tier anywhere except unrelated SDK strings. 4. Inspect requireAdmin() (auth.ts 81-91): only checks the boolean RPC.
bugs.expected: Three distinct tiers (Admin, Manager, User) each with a different, enforced permission set (e.g. Admin manages projects/users, Manager reads analytics, User reads own data).
bugs.actual: Only two effective states exist: admin (admin OR owner — treated identically) and not-admin (member, who is denied all analytics tables by RLS). 'owner' and 'admin' have identical privileges; 'manager' does not exist; 'member' has no usable access. There is no intermediate Manager capability and no per-tier permission matrix.
bugs.fix: Either (a) update the spec/docs to state the system is intentionally a single admin tier, or (b) implement real tiers: convert role to an enum including 'manager', add is_analytics_manager()/role-aware helpers, and add tier-specific RLS policies + a requireRole(min) helper instead of the binary requireAdmin().
bugs.evidence: 0002_core_schema.sql:52 (role default 'member', comment 'member | admin | owner'); 0002_core_schema.sql:248-254 (is_analytics_admin checks only admin/owner); auth.ts:78-91 (requireAdmin only consumes the boolean). Grep for 'manager'/'Manager' returns only packages/sdk and package-lock.json — zero RBAC usage.

bugs.title: Dashboard pages bypass all authorization — render org-wide analytics with no requireAdmin/RLS check
bugs.steps: 1. Open any dashboard page, e.g. dashboard/users/page.tsx — it calls fetchActiveUsers() (line 65) with no auth guard. 2. fetchers.ts: fetchActiveUsers -> getActiveUsers (repositories/analytics.ts). 3. analytics.ts:20 etc. uses getSupabaseAdmin() (service-role, RLS-bypassing). 4. (dashboard)/layout.tsx has no auth check. 5. middleware.ts -> updateSession only refreshes session ('Phase 1 does not gate any routes', supabase/middleware.ts:9).
bugs.expected: Every dashboard surface should verify an authenticated admin (requireAdmin) before rendering, or enforce RLS via a user-context client so non-admins/anonymous users see nothing.
bugs.actual: All dashboard server components fetch via the service-role client which bypasses RLS, and no layer calls requireAdmin(). No route is gated by middleware and there is no login page. Any unauthenticated request that reaches a dashboard route can render full cross-org user/session/analytics data. RLS and requireAdmin() are only enforced on 5 JSON API routes that the UI does not even use for reads.
bugs.fix: Add an auth gate in (dashboard)/layout.tsx (call requireAdmin() / redirect to a login page on failure), and/or gate /dashboard in middleware. The RLS-bypassing service-role path is acceptable only AFTER an authorization check has run for the request.
bugs.evidence: users/page.tsx:64-65 (no guard before fetchActiveUsers); fetchers.ts:123-124; repositories/analytics.ts:2,20,53 (getSupabaseAdmin); supabase/admin.ts:8-16 ('Bypasses RLS'); supabase/middleware.ts:9-10,34 (no gating); (dashboard)/layout.tsx:1-6 (no auth).

bugs.title: RLS self-update policy permits privilege escalation to owner/admin
bugs.steps: 1. Read policy at 0002 line 259: USING (id = auth.uid()) WITH CHECK (id = auth.uid()) on UPDATE, with no column restriction. 2. As any authenticated user with a row in analytics_users, run via a user-context (anon-key + session) client: update analytics_users set role='owner' where id = auth.uid(). 3. is_analytics_admin() now returns true for that user.
bugs.expected: A user may update only safe self-fields (e.g. display_name); the role column must be immutable to self-service updates (admin-only).
bugs.actual: The policy allows updating ANY column of one's own row, including role. A non-admin can escalate to owner/admin. No later migration restricts the role column.
bugs.fix: Restrict the column set: add a BEFORE UPDATE trigger that rejects role changes unless is_analytics_admin(), or split into a column-scoped policy / view. e.g. WITH CHECK (id = auth.uid() AND role = (select role from analytics_users where id = auth.uid())).
bugs.evidence: 0002_core_schema.sql:259 — single policy with no column guard; grep across all migrations confirms no later lockdown of the role column. Today the only thing preventing exploitation is the absence of a UI/API surface, but RLS is the security boundary and it permits the write.

bugs.title: Admin project-creation server action has no admin authorization check

recommendations: Decide and document the intended model. If the product is genuinely single-tier admin, update the spec and docs to say so and drop the 'member' value as a usable role. If three tiers are required, implement them for real (enum with manager, role-aware RLS, requireRole(min) helper).

Close the Critical gap first: add await requireAdmin() at the top of every dashboard Server Action (starting with createProjectAction) and add an admin gate to (dashboard)/layout.tsx (or middleware) so the RLS-bypassing service-role fetch path only runs after authorization.
Add a login/auth surface — there is currently no login page, so the session-based requireAdmin() checks can never be satisfied by a real user in the UI.

Lock down the analytics_users self-update RLS policy so the role column is immutable to non-admin self-service (column-scoped policy or a BEFORE UPDATE trigger), eliminating the privilege-escalation path.

If owner is meant to be a higher tier than admin, add is_analytics_owner()/requireOwner() and route role-management and destructive actions through it; otherwise collapse owner and admin into one role to remove dead distinction.
Build an admin-gated user/role management UI so role assignment does not require manual SQL, making whatever tier model you choose actually operable.
Add automated tests (pgTAP for RLS policies + integration tests for requireAdmin on routes and server actions) to prevent regressions, since the current enforcement is inconsistent across surfaces.

findings.summary: Audited edge cases / validation / boundaries across the ingestion path (events route, parseBody, events schema, events repository), the Add-Project flow (AddProjectForm, createProjectAction, repositories/projects.ts), batch/payload limits (constants/api.ts, config/runtime.ts), and metric repositories (analytics, features, audience, insights, reliability, retention, operational). Verdict: input shape validation is generally solid (strict Zod, slug regex, batch min/max, field-error mapping, empty-state rendering on the projects page). But several real edge-case defects exist: a 32KB payload constant that is silently dead (route enforces a different 64KB cap), a body-size guard that trusts the spoofable/optional content-length header instead of measuring bytes, unregistered portal slugs surfacing as 500s instead of clean 400s, an onboarding flow that can permanently orphan a Postgres enum value on partial failure, three inconsistent slug-length bounds across validators, and no ordering/bounds validation on date ranges or occurredAt. JS-side division-by-zero is well guarded (errorRate, adoption %, pctChange, platformUsage7d all check the denominator); the risk there sits in SQL views I could not execute. Several items are Needs-runtime since I cannot exercise the live DB/UI.

bugs.title: MAX_EVENT_PAYLOAD_BYTES (32KB) is dead code — events route enforces a different 64KB cap
bugs.steps: 1. Read constants/api.ts line 16: export const MAX_EVENT_PAYLOAD_BYTES = 32 * 1024. 2. Grep for its usage. 3. Inspect events route POST: parseBody(req, schema, { maxBytes: RUNTIME.ingest.maxBodyBytes }). 4. RUNTIME.ingest.maxBodyBytes = 64 * 1024 in config/runtime.ts.
bugs.expected: The documented per-batch payload cap is a single source of truth and is the value actually enforced at ingest.
bugs.actual: MAX_EVENT_PAYLOAD_BYTES (32KB) is never imported anywhere; the route enforces RUNTIME.ingest.maxBodyBytes (64KB). The two disagree by 2x and the named constant is misleading dead code. Anyone reasoning about the limit from constants/api.ts will be wrong by half.
bugs.fix: Either delete MAX_EVENT_PAYLOAD_BYTES from constants/api.ts, or make config/runtime.ts derive maxBodyBytes from it (and reconcile to one intended value). Same applies to whether MAX_EVENT_BATCH_SIZE and the runtime config should share one home.
bugs.evidence: constants/api.ts:16 defines 32KB; route.ts:48-50 passes RUNTIME.ingest.maxBodyBytes; runtime.ts:10 sets maxBodyBytes = 64*1024. Grep over repositories/src shows no import of MAX_EVENT_PAYLOAD_BYTES.

bugs.title: Body-size guard trusts the optional/spoofable content-length header instead of measuring actual bytes
bugs.steps: 1. Read parseBody (validate.ts:10-32). 2. Note the only size check: const declared = Number(req.headers.get('content-length') ?? '0'); if declared > maxBytes throw. 3. Then it unconditionally calls await req.json() which buffers the entire body.
bugs.expected: A request whose real body exceeds maxBytes is rejected before the full payload is buffered/parsed, regardless of the client-declared content-length.
bugs.actual: If content-length is absent (chunked/streamed) it defaults to '0' and the check passes; if a client lies and sends a small content-length the check also passes. Either way req.json() then reads the whole body into memory. The maxBytes cap is advisory only and is bypassable, so the route's DoS/oversized-payload protection is weaker than intended. The batch is still bounded to 50 events by the schema, but each event allows url/referrer up to 2048 chars plus arbitrary metadata (z.record(z.string(), z.unknown())) with no per-field metadata size cap, so a 50-event batch of large metadata blobs can far exceed 64KB and is only stopped if the client honestly declares content-length.
bugs.fix: Read the body as text/ArrayBuffer and check its real byte length (Buffer.byteLength) before JSON.parse, or stream with a running byte counter that aborts past maxBytes. Do not rely solely on the content-length header. Consider also bounding metadata size in trackEventSchema.
bugs.evidence: validate.ts:15-26 — only header is checked, then raw = await req.json() runs regardless; schemas/events.ts:51 metadata is z.record(z.string(), z.unknown()) with no size bound; :49-50 url/referrer are max 2048 each.

bugs.title: Events for an unregistered portal slug return 500 INGEST_FAILED instead of a clean 4xx
bugs.steps: 1. portalIdSchema (schemas/events.ts:14-18) accepts any slug matching ^[a-z][a-z0-9_-]*$ up to 64 chars — it validates SHAPE, not existence. 2. analytics_events.portal_id is public.portal_id (an enum) NOT NULL REFERENCES analytics_portals(id) (0002_core_schema.sql:103). 3. Send POST /api/v1/events with a valid global API key and an event whose portalId is a well-formed but never-onboarded slug (e.g. 'ghost-app'). 4. insertEventsBatch maps portal_id: e.portalId and inserts.
bugs.expected: A well-formed but unknown portalId is rejected with a 400/422 (clear 'unknown project' message) so SDKs can correct their config.
bugs.actual: Postgres rejects the row: the slug is not a member of the portal_id enum (and/or violates the analytics_portals FK), so insert throws and is wrapped as AppError('INGEST_FAILED', ..., 500). The whole batch fails with a generic 500, masking a caller configuration error as a server fault. ensureSessionsForBatch likewise can 500 on SESSION_UPSERT_FAILED. Note the auth layer accepts the global INGEST_API_KEY for ANY portalId, so this is reachable by any holder of the shared key.
bugs.fix: Before insert, look up the set of registered slugs (getProjectBySlug / analytics_portals) for the distinct portalIds in the batch and return a 400/422 ValidationError naming the unknown slug(s). Alternatively map Postgres invalid-enum/FK violation codes (22P02 / 23503) to a 400 in insertEventsBatch.
bugs.evidence: schemas/events.ts:14-18 (regex-only slug); 0002_core_schema.sql:103 (portal_id enum + FK NOT NULL); events.ts:132-157 inserts portal_id verbatim and throws 500 on any error; auth.ts:39-42 global key matches regardless of portal.

bugs.title: createProject can permanently orphan a Postgres enum value on partial failure
bugs.steps: 1. createProject calls admin.rpc('add_portal_value', { p_slug: slug }) (projects.ts:118) which executes ALTER TYPE portal_id ADD VALUE IF NOT EXISTS (migration 0017:50-58) in its own transaction. 2. It then upserts analytics_portals (line 122) and inserts analytics_projects (line 129). 3. If either of those later steps fails (DB error, constraint, transient outage), the function throws — but the enum value added in step 1 has already committed.
bugs.expected: A failed onboarding leaves no partial state; retrying with the same or a corrected slug is clean.
bugs.actual: The enum value is added in a separate committed transaction and Postgres cannot drop an enum value, so a failure in step 2/3 leaves a dangling portal_id enum member with no analytics_portals row and no analytics_projects row. The enum permanently accumulates orphans. A retry of the same slug re-runs add_portal_value (IF NOT EXISTS, harmless) but the user sees a 500 with no created project; an admin cannot clean up the enum value via the app.
bugs.fix: Reorder so the irreversible enum grow happens last, or wrap steps 2-3 in a single transaction and only grow the enum after they succeed, or insert the registry/portal rows first (these are reversible) and grow the enum as the final committed step. Document that orphan enum values require manual DBA cleanup.
bugs.evidence: projects.ts:117-146 (enum grown first, then upsert, then insert, each able to throw); migration 0017:50-58 add_portal_value uses ALTER TYPE ADD VALUE (irreversible).

bugs.title: Inconsistent slug length/shape bounds across the three validators
bugs.steps: 1. portalIdSchema: min(1) max(64), regex ^[a-z][a-z0-9_-]*$ (events ingest). 2. createProjectAction inputSchema.slug: min(2) max(63), regex ^[a-z][a-z0-9_-]*$ (admin form). 3. createProject SLUG_RE = ^[a-z][a-z0-9_-]{1,62}$ i.e. total length 2..63 (repository). Compare the accepted sets.
bugs.expected: A slug accepted at creation is exactly the set of slugs accepted at event ingest, with one consistent length bound.
bugs.actual: Three different bounds: ingest allows length 1..64 (a single-letter slug like 'a' and 64-char slugs are valid for events), but creation requires 2..63. So a 64-char slug can never be created yet would be accepted by the ingest schema (and then 500 because it's not registered — see the unknown-portal bug). A 1-char slug is ingest-valid but un-creatable. The form-level vs repo-level bounds happen to align at 2..63, but the ingest path diverges, which is confusing and can produce 'valid event slug that no project can own'.
bugs.fix: Define one slug schema (length and regex) in schemas/events.ts and import it in both actions.ts and projects.ts (replace the hand-rolled SLUG_RE and the duplicated regex/length in inputSchema). Pick a single max (63 or 64) and a single min.

bugs.title: No ordering or bounds validation on date inputs (from > to, future/ancient occurredAt)
bugs.steps: 1. analyticsQuerySchema (schemas/events.ts:64-72) validates from/to as z.string().datetime() independently — no check that from <= to. 2. trackEventSchema.occurredAt (line 52) is only z.string().datetime().optional() — no upper/lower bound. 3. insertEventsBatch (events.ts:147) writes occurred_at: e.occurredAt ?? new Date().toISOString() verbatim.
bugs.expected: from > to yields an empty/explicitly-rejected range; client-supplied occurredAt is clamped or rejected when implausibly future-dated or far in the past (to protect time-bucketed views/partitions and KPI windows).
bugs.actual: A client can submit from later than to (analytics queries silently return empty or driver-error depending on the view), and can backdate or future-date events arbitrarily (e.g. occurredAt = '2999-01-01T00:00:00Z'). Future-dated events land in current 24h/7d/28d KPI and time-series windows incorrectly and can target partitions that may not exist (partition maintenance only pre-creates leadMonths=2 ahead per runtime.ts:30), risking insert failures for far-future dates. getEventsTimeSeries buckets by hour and silently drops rows outside the window, so backdated data can vanish from charts without warning.
bugs.fix: Add a .refine on analyticsQuerySchema that from <= to. Bound occurredAt in trackEventSchema (e.g. reject > now + small skew, and older than retention horizon) or clamp server-side in insertEventsBatch. Ensure far-future occurredAt cannot hit a missing partition.
bugs.evidence: schemas/events.ts:52 (occurredAt unbounded), :68-69 (from/to independent, no refine); events.ts:147 writes occurredAt verbatim; analytics.ts:138-176 window-buckets and drops out-of-window rows; runtime.ts:28-31 leadMonths=2.

bugs.title: userName allowed up to 200 chars but no trim/normalization; userEmail case handled inconsistently for enrichment
bugs.steps: 1. trackEventSchema.userEmail is .email().max(320) (good). 2. resolveUserIds lowercases email for the resolve/mint key (events.ts:49,65,93,114) — consistent. 3. But the uuid-enrichment update writes cur.email = e.userEmail.toLowerCase() to analytics_users.email only when currently null (line 72), guarded by .is('email', null); on email-collision it is swallowed (line 74-76).
bugs.expected: Two events in one batch — one with userId+userEmail and another email-only event for the SAME person — converge to one user row.
bugs.actual: An event carrying userId enriches that uuid row's email, while an email-only event mints a DIFFERENT deterministic uuidv5-from-email row (events.ts:97-104). These are two distinct analytics_users rows for the same human; there is no merge. This is an identity edge case rather than a crash, but it inflates active-user counts and splits a person's history across two ids. The collision path on the enrichment UPDATE is silently swallowed so the operator gets no signal.
bugs.fix: Document/accept the split, or add a reconciliation step that links the uuidv5-from-email synthetic id to the directory uuid when both an email and a uuid for the same lower(email) are seen. At minimum, count distinct humans by resolved canonical id, not raw user_id.
bugs.evidence: events.ts:97-104 mints uuidv5FromEmail rows; :70-77 enriches uuid rows separately with collision swallowed; the two id spaces never merge.

recommendations: Replace the content-length-only check in parseBody with a real byte-length measurement (read text/ArrayBuffer, check Buffer.byteLength before JSON.parse, or stream with an aborting counter). The current cap is bypassable and the body is buffered regardless.

Validate portalId existence at ingest: resolve the distinct slugs in the batch against the registry and return 400/422 for unknown slugs, instead of letting a Postgres enum/FK violation surface as a 500 INGEST_FAILED.

Reorder createProject so the irreversible add_portal_value enum grow is the last committed step (or wrap the reversible portal/registry writes in one transaction first). Postgres cannot drop enum values, so the current ordering permanently orphans them on partial failure.

Consolidate slug validation into one shared schema imported by schemas/events.ts, actions.ts, and projects.ts — the three currently disagree on min/max (1..64 vs 2..63), allowing event-valid slugs that no project can own.

Add date sanity to schemas: refine analyticsQuerySchema so from <= to, and bound trackEventSchema.occurredAt (reject far-future / far-past) so KPI windows, hour-bucketing, and partitioning stay correct.

Reconcile the payload limits: MAX_EVENT_PAYLOAD_BYTES (32KB) is dead while the route enforces RUNTIME.ingest.maxBodyBytes (64KB). Pick one source of truth, and consider bounding event.metadata size since z.record(...,z.unknown()) is unbounded per field.

Fix the misleading name regex message: ^[a-z0-9._-]+$ with the i flag actually permits uppercase, contradicting the 'must be lowercase' message in schemas/events.ts:41 — either drop the i flag or correct the message.

Confirm and document event idempotency: insertEventsBatch uses .insert (not upsert) on a client-supplied id, so retried batches with the same id will hit a PK violation -> 500, contradicting the 'idempotent retries' comment. Switch to upsert with onConflict:'id' ignoreDuplicates if idempotency is intended.

Decide how 'unknown' clientIp callers should be treated by the rate limiter — they currently all share a single bucket, which can either over-throttle legitimate proxied traffic or be exploited; consider per-key fallbacks.
